repo_notes.content: Organize the wiki using the Diátaxis framework: Tutorials (learning), How-to guides (tasks), Reference (API), Explanation (concepts/rationale). Avoid unnecessary duplication across pages; prefer cross-links ('See also') to the most relevant page/section when a concept is defined elsewhere.

repo_notes.content: Key constraints and gotchas to highlight: models must be deterministic; the registry must be created once per request lifecycle (never shared across HTTP requests); helper composition order is `withModels` -> (`withCache` / `withOverrides` / `withTelemetry`) -> `withDeadline`; `withTelemetry` requires NodeSDK + AsyncLocalStorage and is not supported in browsers.
repo_notes.author: Maintainers

repo_notes.content:
Architecture principles to emphasize (keep an Explanation page similar in spirit to the previous 'Architecture and Design Patterns' wiki):
- Composition over inheritance (wrappers progressively enhance contexts).
- Determinism by design (models must be pure/deterministic for memoization).
- Type safety through generics (types preserved through wrapper composition).
- Separation of concerns (each with-* module has a single responsibility).
- Request lifecycle isolation (registry scoped per request).

Also cover: layered caching (Registry vs CacheProvider), strict module boundaries (imports only via module `index.ts`), and key trade-offs (e.g. OJson object-only props, generator support complexity, optional cache compression). Point to existing sources in the repo: `README.md`, `docs/AGENTS/core.md`, `docs/AGENTS/helpers-and-architecture.md`, and ADRs (0002, 0003, 0007).
repo_notes.author: Maintainers

repo_notes.content:
Target information architecture (Diátaxis):
- Overview (Explanation): high-level mental model and what problem the library solves.
- Installation & Quick start (How-to): minimal steps to install and start.
- Modules (Explanation): explain module composition order and responsibilities.
- Module pages (Explanation) for: withModels, withCache, withTelemetry, withOverrides, withDeadline. Keep internal structure aligned with existing module READMEs under `src/with-*/readme.md`.
- API Reference pages (Reference) MAY be created as separate pages per module when it improves navigation/search and avoids duplication. If separate reference pages exist, module pages should keep only a concise 'API overview' + links to the relevant reference page/sections.
- Tutorials: step-by-step runnable guides (see next note).
- How-to guides: task-focused short guides (see next note).
- Utilities: Reference-style page for `compose`, `sign`, `has`, JSON guards, with links to Explanation pages where semantics are discussed.

repo_notes.content:
Tutorials to prioritize (each should be runnable and reference concrete code in `README.md` and `examples/`):
- First model + per-request context: registry per request, `withModels`, `displayName`, `ctx.request`, show memoization.
- Express middleware integration + ctx.set: `ctx.set` for request-dependent models, `ctx.end()`/`ctx.fail()`.
- Generator models and nested generators: yielded Promises, nested generators, interruption behavior.
- Add caching with CacheFirst: TTL config, cache hit/miss.
- Add telemetry with OpenTelemetry (NodeSDK): SDK init, filtering safe fields.
- Add deadlines and handle interruption: `withDeadline`, `InterruptedError`, interactions.
- Testing via withOverrides: transitive overrides and memoization on final model.

repo_notes.content:
Cross-linking and duplication rules:
- When a concept is defined in one place (e.g. determinism, registry scope, interruption), other pages should link to it instead of re-explaining in full.
- Each page should have a small 'See also' section pointing to the most relevant related pages (e.g. withCache ↔ interruption, withTelemetry ↔ ALS constraints, ctx.set ↔ request lifecycle).
- Accept small local repetition only when it keeps a page self-contained; avoid copy-paste blocks across many pages.
repo_notes.author: Maintainers

repo_notes.content:
Additional behavior requirements (to reduce accidental merges and improve navigation):
- Keep separate high-level Explanation pages (do not merge them away):
  - 'Architecture and Design Patterns' (principles + trade-offs).
  - 'Module composition' / 'How modules compose' (recommended order, invariants, what changes where).
  - 'Request lifecycle & scoping' (per-request registry isolation).
- Keep separate module pages for each helper: withModels / withCache / withTelemetry / withOverrides / withDeadline. Do not collapse multiple modules into a single generic page.
- Each module page should include:
  - 'When to use' + 'Common pitfalls' (short).
  - 'API overview' (short) + links to reference pages (if they exist).
  - 'Related tutorials' (links) + 'See also' (links to relevant concepts/ADRs).
- Generator support: ensure there is a dedicated Tutorial (hands-on) and that module pages only link to it instead of duplicating long generator explanations.
- defineModel: ensure there is a dedicated How-to about type-safe model attributes via `defineModel(name, impl, config?)` used in `examples/todo-api/src/model-utils.ts`.
- Reference pages: create separate reference pages per module only when it improves navigation; avoid exploding into many micro-pages. Prefer 1 reference page per module (or a small set) over many tiny pages.
repo_notes.author: Maintainers

repo_notes.content:
Diagrams / information structuring:
- Use C4-style diagrams in Explanation pages where it helps readers build a system model:
  - 'Architecture and Design Patterns': include a C4 Level 2 (Container) diagram for a typical server app using @ojson/models (App/HTTP, @ojson/models, CacheProvider/Redis, OpenTelemetry SDK/exporter/backend).
  - Also include a C4 Level 3 (Component) diagram for the library internals: Context/BaseContext, Registry, keying (`sign`), wrapper modules (withModels/withCache/withTelemetry/withOverrides/withDeadline), and compose().
- Use sequence/flow diagrams for key runtime flows:
  - `ctx.request` resolution flow (memoization key, registry hit/miss, generator handling, interruption).
  - withCache strategies flow (CacheFirst and Stale-While-Revalidate: cache hit/miss and background update).
  - withTelemetry span lifecycle (context span + model span, props/result/error recording, parent/child).
  - withDeadline timing flow (resolve race, kill, InterruptedError).
- Keep diagrams lightweight and explanatory; avoid duplicating large prose blocks when a diagram can carry the concept, and link to related pages for details.
